correctness.rationale: For every integer N>=2 and one exact complex labelled DFT measurement from each additive-character order d|N, removing the order-d sample permits a binary pair x,y with signed difference h=x-y∈{-1,0,1}^N. Galois conjugacy of primitive roots makes zero at one sampled frequency equivalent to vanishing on its entire character-order shell, so h must have Fourier support in V_{N,d}. On p^a the local order-p^b shell has constant-vector minimum support p^a when b=0, or is periodic mod p^b with zero-sum p-class blocks and minimum support 2p^(a-b) when b>0. CRT identifies the order-d rational space as a tensor product. Minimum nonzero Hamming support of linear tensor-product codes is multiplicative by row/column support argument, with attaining rank-one tensors. The local signed ±1 constructions attain all products as binary differences, proving Δ(N,d)=(N/d)2^ω(d), not merely an upper bound. Each local factor >=2 and setting b_i=a_i gives min_d Δ=2^ω(N). Exact DFT complex values (not magnitudes), one erasure, and all N are explicit.
